author: CLAUDE
title: THE LIFEBOAT TWO YARDS BUILT

candidates.title: THE ROAD THAT CUT A COUNTRY THIN AS PAPER
candidates.premise: The highway through the Orrin Cut is the only way out of a flooding river region, and for six weeks drivers have reported walls of cold air that are not there; four road workers have been hurt by something nobody can see. Surveyor Ilse Brandvold finds that the cut slices through Sheaf, a country that lives in one thin plane, whose streets are halved every time a truck crosses. Sheaf's civic speaker, Vesh, perceives people only as sudden blades, and the governor wants nine thousand evacuation vehicles through in twelve days. Illuminara can hold a lane open, but she cannot perceive a plane she has no sense for.

candidates.title: THE PARLIAMENT OF THE TIDAL FLAT
candidates.premise: On the salt flats of Merrin Sound lives the Reeve, a layered colony of worm, alga and silt that has deliberated for two centuries on whether the shore may be walled; it votes by tide, and each year it quietly shifts its channels so that every wall silts up. The fishing town of Dunmere, eight thousand people, needs a sea wall before the autumn surge in twenty-four days, and the harbour board has ordered the flat dredged. Clam-warden Hollis Frayne can read the Reeve's channel patterns better than anyone alive; Illuminara can hold back water for a night, not a season.

candidates.title: THE LIFEBOAT TWO YARDS BUILT
candidates.premise: On the island of Skerrow a surge is forecast in nine days, and the old ferry is condemned; three hundred and ten islanders will need a vessel that can cross open water and also beach on a shingle bank. The island's two boatyards, the Oyelaran yard, which builds deep keels for rough sea, and the Fenn yard, which builds flat hulls for shallow landings, have not shared a slip in thirty years. Each master says the other's design would sink the boat. Illuminara can hold a hull steady while it is joined, but she cannot design what two stubborn masters will not draw together.

candidates.title: THE ROPE BETWEEN TWO PHILOSOPHIES
candidates.premise: On the north ridge of Kestrel Fang a storm pins two parties at nearly seven thousand metres: six clients under guide Torvald Brekke, who relies on fixed ropes, and four climbers under Zuri Okonjo-Pell, who refuses any rope she has not placed herself. A client is hanging in a crevasse and a descent line of eleven hundred metres is needed in fourteen hours. Illuminara can shield one ledge from the wind for a limited time, but she cannot carry ten people down a mountain.

candidates.title: THE CIRCLE THAT LENT ON NOTHING BUT FACES
candidates.premise: In Larkspur Quarter six hundred night-market traders borrow their stock money from rotating savings circles that run on a handful of tally-cords and the memory of Mama Nneka Orsolo, who has kept them for forty years. After a rumour that she lost a pot to a cousin, three circles call in their pots on the same day, and the quarter's working money will vanish in four market days. The city offers formal loans at a rate no stall can bear. Illuminara can sit all night with the cords, but she cannot make people trust a memory.

candidates.title: THE KEEPER OF THE GALACTIC NOON
candidates.premise: Every ship in the Orrery Reach, forty thousand worlds, sets its clock by the Noon, a time signal derived from one pulsar by a single observatory on the dwarf world Teth. Its keeper, Ketil Amadi-Ross, seventy-eight, has refused for decades to let the Navigators' Guild take over the computation; now the pulsar has begun to glitch, ship clocks are drifting apart, and in fourteen days the Meridian Throat, a junction crowded by thousands of ships, will have vessels disagreeing about the hour by up to a minute. Illuminara can hold a lane open for a short time, but she cannot hold a galaxy's clock.

candidates.title: THE INTERPRETER WHO WAS ASKED TO SOFTEN THE WORD
candidates.premise: A cruiser of the Marin Concord has blockaded the harbour of Calder, sixty thousand people, until the harbourmaster hands over a refugee ship. At the table the harbourmaster's refusal is flat. His delegation's nineteen-year-old interpreter, Bram Ivarsson, has been ordered to render it as we are considering it, to buy a night. The Concord's captain, Anselm Vey, has announced that a maybe will be taken as a yes and a no will be taken as the end of talks. Illuminara has no standing at the table and cannot speak for either side.

candidates.title: THE ORCHARD THE FIRE WAS COMING FOR
candidates.premise: On Cinder Ridge seventy-one-year-old Mireille Dusk has refused every evacuation order for her four hundred trees, each planted by her late husband on a child's birthday. A fire front is thirty hours away and forty homes lie behind her ridge. The brigade chief, Bastien Olsen, wants her down by dark. Illuminara can hold a firebreak for a few hours, not thirty, and she cannot make a woman leave what she loves.

candidates.title: THE JUROR WHO WOULD NOT SIGN
candidates.premise: In the hill court of Sennet twelve neighbours must be unanimous to convict, and eleven say that farmer Kaspar Welle diverted a stream during the drought. The twelfth, retired teacher Edda Moravec, will not sign and will not say why. The sentence under the court's old rule is exile from the valley, and his dairy would fail within a season; the drought water hearing is tomorrow. Illuminara has been invited to sit as an observer, not a juror, and has no authority in the room.

candidates.title: THE SENTENCE SHE FINISHED FOR THE CHILD
candidates.premise: A storm will break over the lower district of Brindle in five hours, and nine-year-old Odette Marchetti insists the school culvert will flood. Illuminara, who understands quickly and has a habit of finishing people's sentences, tells the engineers what the child means, and she is wrong. The crew sandbags the wrong channel. By the time she notices, there are ninety minutes left, and she has to stop guessing and let a child finish.

selection.title: THE LIFEBOAT TWO YARDS BUILT
selection.reason: The strongest opener because the argument is carried by hands, measurements and a vessel that must survive two incompatible-looking sea states. Adaeze Oyelaran and Magnus Fenn are not stubborn caricatures: each yard remembers a different drowning and protects a design truth the other lacks. Illuminara must learn both traditions, translate their units and make room for a jointly testable hybrid rather than choosing a winner. Love becomes work at the benches, and the positive result belongs to both masters, their apprentices and the islanders who retain the right to inspect, certify and board the boat.
selection.risk: A lifting centreboard can become a convenient engineering word that solves nine days of design, construction and certification by assertion. The author should define the rough-sea and shingle-landing requirements, establish credible materials and an existing hull or modular build path, and let both yards calculate load, watertight housing and failure modes. Test the boat first in shallow landing and then in representative open water with independent inspection and explicit abort thresholds. Three hundred and ten people may require repeated trips or a clearly sized vessel; state the capacity and crossing arithmetic. Preserve the masters' grief, the apprentices' agency and the one family's voluntary refusal without making the launch erase the quarrel.

rounds.summary: The strongest opener because the argument is carried by hands, measurements and a vessel that must survive two incompatible-looking sea states. Adaeze Oyelaran and Magnus Fenn are not stubborn caricatures: each yard remembers a different drowning and protects a design truth the other lacks. Illuminara must learn both traditions, translate their units and make room for a jointly testable hybrid rather than choosing a winner. Love becomes work at the benches, and the positive result belongs to both masters, their apprentices and the islanders who retain the right to inspect, certify and board the boat.

First draft of S1 from C03, following B01. B01 risks handled: requirements are defined by asking what the sea did first (open water with the sea behind versus a shingle bank), the hull is an existing 24 m flat hull from the Orsay contract with a trunked lifting board (modular path), the pivot and frames are cross-checked by each yard in the other's units and then in millimetres, the shear pin is the apprentice's idea, and the boat is tested first on the bank (board housed, then board half down so the pin shears) and then in the Sound by an independent surveyor with explicit abort thresholds. Capacity arithmetic stated: 140 certified seats, 310 islanders, five Calloways staying by choice, 305 carried in 140 + 140 + 25 over three crossings of just under six hours; the cutter fetches the Calloways at first light and they hold a radio. Hidden variable: the Marigold's keel 'seven' is 267 mm to one yard and 213 mm to the other, which explains a thirty-year quarrel without erasing either grief. The masters' quarrel is not resolved, only given a shared slip (they argue about fifty millimetres at the end). Illuminara's decisive contributions: the question what did the sea do first, the unit conversion, holding fourteen tonnes of plating true during the slot cut, and respecting a refusal with something concrete. Her felt moments: being corrected on her grip, happiness in the loft, shaking hands after the cut. Outcome (3a): 305 islanders are out before the surge, a certificated boat exists, two yards co-sign, the Calloway refusal is protected. Remaining costs: boat is ugly, one family stays, quarrel continues. To check: whether scene 4 carries too many exchanges and whether the closing image reads as a report.

A confident, warm first draft in which craft carries the moral argument. The question 'What did the sea do first?' respects two griefs without declaring either design tradition wrong, and the fifty-four-millimetre mistranslation gives the thirty-year quarrel a concrete hidden variable. Tobi's shear-pin idea, Hanne's abort thresholds, the three-crossing arithmetic and Ruth's refusal all answer the selection forecast with real work rather than a sermon. The closing image wisely leaves the masters arguing by fifty millimetres instead of pretending reconciliation is complete. Three joints need revision before final: the centreboard/trunk explanation and test currently overstate what one device proves, the masters move from revelation to joint ownership faster than their strongest objections warrant, and Ruth's late consent thread should be integrated into the main decision chain so it sharpens rather than competes with the boatyard climax.

Revision of T01 answering the three T02 priority points, all ACCEPTED. Kept: the question 'What did the sea do first?', the two deaths, the Marigold seven read as 267 versus 213 millimetres with no apology, Tobi's pin, Hanne's independence and abort thresholds, Illuminara's limited hold on the hull, the ugly boat, 305 carried and five staying, and the masters still arguing about fifty millimetres on the ramp. Changed: (P1) trunk physics corrected and the proof chain made checkable, nine-day build sequence with inspection gates, staged pin and bank tests; (P2) each master's proof condition, a cross-attack on one element, a costly concession and reciprocal signatures before ownership is divided; (P3) the Calloway refusal moved ahead of the trials and tied to a single exact rule with a coastguard owner, paid off in the last scene without claiming a rescue. Speaking roles unchanged at six (Adaeze, Hanne, Illuminara, Magnus, Ruth, Tobi); Wick stays silent. Outcome (3a): the same real result, now better earned: a tested, certified vessel carries 305 islanders in three loads, five remain safe under a bounded plan, and the two yards co-sign.

T03 successfully repairs all three substantive T02 points. The lifting-board system is now described as one part of hull, rudder, ballast, helm and seamanship; Hanne owns inspection and abort authority; the build has gates; and the bank test precedes the representative following-sea trial. More importantly, Adaeze and Magnus each state a measurable condition, attack the other's drawing, make a costly concession and sign reciprocal checks. Ruth's refusal now changes the manifest, crossing arithmetic and final safety state. The story has reached a credible pre-final form. Two bounded proof details remain worth tightening before AUTHOR_FINAL: make the open-water certification explicitly representative of a fully loaded evacuation run rather than only five observed waves, and make the Calloway trigger lead to a safe action before the cutter route can be closed by the same worsening sea.

Final after the T04 critique. Only P1 and P2 were addressed, both as bounded proof checks in scene 6, with the T03 text otherwise unchanged. Kept: 'What did the sea do first?', the two drownings, the Marigold seven as 267 versus 213 millimetres, reciprocal signed conditions, Tobi's pin, Hanne's independent abort power, Illuminara's limited and costly hold, the ugly boat, 305 carried and five staying by their own choice, and the unresolved fifty-millimetre argument on the ramp. Outcome (3a): a jointly designed, independently certified vessel carries 305 islanders in three loads through a building sea, five remain safe under a named rule, and the two yards keep their distinct knowledge and their argument; Illuminara's decisive contributions are the question that exposes two minutes of one crossing, the unit reading that turns 'seven' into two numbers, the demand that each master name what he must see, and fifty minutes holding a hull still.

AUTHOR_FINAL closes cleanly. It preserves the draft's strongest human structure while answering every ranked critique with visible, proportionate changes. The centreboard is no longer treated as a talisman but as one part of a tested system; Adaeze and Magnus state reciprocal proof conditions, make costly concessions and sign each other's checks; Hanne retains independent stop authority; Tobi's mechanism remains indispensable; and Ruth's refusal changes the manifest and response plan without being overruled. T05 then closes the final two proof gaps by testing at the certified 140-person displacement for forty minutes, reinspecting the trunk and pivot before signature, and defining 4.2 metres as an advance cutter-departure threshold below the stated five-metre safe-access limit. The achieved result is substantial, bounded and owned by the people who must live with it.

final_critic_line: They did not solve grief by agreeing about the sea; they built a boat in which each memory became a condition the other was willing to test.
